scope: Proposition 5.4 (Scalar-normal first jet) of the manuscript “Every four-dimensional Kakeya set has full Hausdorff dimension” (preprints/Every-four-dimensional-Kakeya-set-has-full-Hausdorff-dimension-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 074 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 30d0c186aa9c697d), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 76. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Assume Definition 5.2. Fix a finite nested hierarchy of dyadic time lengths of fixed positive power, with finest length H∗. If the available floor is sufficiently fine—ζ ≤ H3 ∗ /K suffices after enlarging K—then a dense restriction of the single-time labels admits a time-only row A(t), bounded by K, such that |F(v) − F(u) − (v − u)A(u)| ≤ KH11/10 (5.15) whenever the retained active times u, v lie in the same designated interval of length H. Put J1(l, t) = x′ l(t) − F(t)y′ l − A(t)yl(t). For every finite presampled tuple and every dense tested event as in Lemma 5.3, on which all tested times carry the retained labels, H(J1(l, t)r | T, Sl(t)r) = o∗ if r ≥ H (1−d)/64 ∗ (5.16) at the available resolutions. The row A and the single-time restriction are fixed before the tuple and the later event are chosen.
